 Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.5582/2022 That on 24.09.2022 at about 9.00 a.m, when the Petitioner was proceeding as a pedestrian on Bengaluru - Kanakapura road, Uttarahalli hobli, Bengaluru, at that time, one motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291 ridden by its rider came in a high speed and ridden extreme right side which overtaking the BMTC bus and dashed against the Petitioner who stands on the extreme side of footpath road and caused the accident.
Due to which the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to CURA hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgery.

She had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/
towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
4. Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was doing Tutor work and was earning 20,000/ per month.
The said accident has occurred due to SCCH 15 4 MVC No.5582/2022 the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18 EJ1291 by its rider.

The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and therefore both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Written statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Written statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it contended that, SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5582/2022 the Petitioner herself attributed her negligence for causing the said accident.
Further it contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle did not possess a valid driving license to ride the motorcycle.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

On these grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

2 6.
On the rival Pleadings, this Court has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 24.09.2022 at about 9.00 a.m. near Somanahalli gate, Bengaluru - Kanakapura road, Uttrahalli hobli, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18 EJ1291 by its rider?
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P11.
Further, she examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.12 and 13 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the written Arguments filed by the Petitioner and depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order, for the following :

SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5582/2022  REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291 by its rider.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ 1291 by its rider.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 and she has reiterated the Petition averments in her Chiefaffidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P6 are the True copies of Amrutha.J vs Manjunatha.V on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52454442/

is the Discharge SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5582/2022 summary.

is the Medical bill.
Ex.P11 is the Aadhaar card.

12. Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR & Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the father of the Petitioner by name Shashidhar Julajuli, the Kaggalipura Police have registered the case against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.

Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate of the Petitioner which shows the following injury:
1) Swelling of right lower limb, fracture comminuted mid shaft closed fracture SCCH 15 9 MVC No.5582/2022 13.
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.

Ex.P.6 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Kaggalipura Police Station against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
14.

"  24.09.2022    9.00
15. Ex.P9 is the Discharge summary and Ex.P10 is the Medical bill.

Further, the Petitioner has examined Doctor by name Dr. S. Ramachandra as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.12 and 13.

4 16.
P.W.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of the PW.1.

Though PW.1 admitted the suggestion that the accident was occurred while she trying to cross the road to board the bus, Ex.P3 - Spot mahazar shows the accident spot is on the footpath in front of the Sweet home.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence.

Under such circumstances, this SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5582/2022 Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291 by its rider and in the said accident, she had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
17. Issue No.2:
As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 19 years.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card at Ex.P11, which shows her date of birth was 16.12.2003.
The accident has taken place on 24.09.2022.
Hence, at the time of accident, the Petitioner was aged about 19 years.

19. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, she was working as Tutor and was earning 20,000/
per month.
But, she has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, SCCH 15 12 MVC No.5582/2022 in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/ per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
21.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 issued by the Medical Officer of the CURA hospital,
Whitefield, shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) swelling of right lower limb, comminuted mid shaft closed fracture SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5582/2022
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.
22. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of 30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
II. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
23. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 20,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
Amrutha.J vs Manjunatha.

V on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52454442/
5 24.

The Petitioner deposed in his evidence that he had taken treatment at CURA hospital,
Koramangala.
Upon going through Ex.P.9  Discharge summary of CURA hospital shows SCCH 15 14 MVC No.5582/2022 that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 26.09.2022 to 28.09.2022.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 03 days.
25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 15,500/ under this head (@ 15,500/ per month ).
IV.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

26. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 3,000/ (@ 100/ per day) towards SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5582/2022 attendants charges, 3,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and 3,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 9,000/ under this head.

V.COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
27.
The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, he had spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced medical bill and hospital bill marked at Ex.P10.
I have gone through the same and the same is acceptable.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,20,000/ under this head.
VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:

28. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5582/2022 disablement and she is not able to do her work as she used to do earlier.
Even in her evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

29. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. S. Ramachandra as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by her at CURA hospital.
Further, he assessed the whole body disability at 18.91%.
PW.2 got marked Outpatient record and Xray at Ex.P12 and 13.
In the crossexamination, he has deposed that, he is not the treated doctor.
Petitioner has taken treatment at CURA hospital and he did not get the opinion of the treated doctors while assessing the disability of the Petitioner.
Further he admitted that the fracture of tibia was partly united.

Further he admitted that the operation was conducted in respect of tibia fracture and there was no operation in respect of fibula fracture and said fracture does not need any SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5582/2022 operation.
He further admitted that fibula is the supporting bone of tibia.

Further he admitted that he himself and treated doctors not Amrutha.J vs Manjunatha.V on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52454442/
6 given disability certificate.

sentences.text: Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of 15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to 3,34,800/ (15,500/ x 12 =
1,86,000/, 1,86,000/x 18 x 10/100 = 3,34,800/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 3,34,800/ under this head.
SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5582/2022 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:

31. To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000 /
2. Loss of amenities  20,000/
3. Loss of income during the laid  15,500/ up period 4. Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  9,000/ and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  1,20,000/
6. Loss of Future Income 3,34,800/ Total 5,29,300/
32.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 5,29,300/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash SCCH 15 19 MVC No.5582/2022 and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the Offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA18EJ1291.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5582/2022 Amrutha.J vs Manjunatha.V on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52454442/
7  The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 5,29,300/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Out of the compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification.
The remaining 50% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the SCCH 15 21 MVC No.5582/2022 Petitioner in any Nationalized or Schedule bank for a period of three years.

The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
